findings.issue: Fill() chooses WHICH paragraphs receive the body correctly (the list is built from the template text before ReplaceAll), but it then recomputes the insertion INDEX with `LetterOpenXml.TextOf(paragraph)` AFTER the eight simple marks have been substituted. If a template writes another mark on the same line as the body mark (e.g. «الموضوع: @اسم الموضوع — @نص المراسلة») and the letter's own value for that mark contains the words «@نص المراسلة» (the head of office quoting the convention in a subject line), `at` lands inside the substituted subject: the letter's text is poured into the subject and RemoveMark then strips the words out of it. LetterComposerTests.Compose_never_pours_the_letter_into_its_own_words covers the value being in a DIFFERENT paragraph, not the same one.
findings.fix: In Fill(), record the body mark's index at the same moment the paragraph is added to bodyParagraphs (before ReplaceAll), then splice a private sentinel — e.g. ￹ — in place of the mark at that index, run ReplaceAll, and let LetterBodyWriter.Insert use the sentinel's position. Store the pair (paragraph, index) in bodyParagraphs instead of the paragraph alone.

findings.issue: Fill(line, values) (the plain-text helper, line 377) substitutes the nine marks by chained string.Replace over LetterMarks.ByLength, so a value inserted for an earlier mark is re-scanned by a later one — a subject of «@رقم الصادر» would be rewritten into the number. FillHtml (line 405), which produces what is actually printed, scans '@' positions and does not have this flaw, so today the defect only affects the blankness and prefix/suffix-length checks; it becomes a real printing defect the moment Fill's result is emitted.
findings.fix: Rewrite Fill as a single left-to-right scan over the line (the same loop FillHtml uses, without the escaping and <bdi>), advancing past each substituted value rather than restarting a Replace per mark; or express both as one scan with a formatting callback.

findings.issue: Measure() computes `usedOnLast = used % contentHeight` whenever the document overflows one page or contains an explicit page break. When `used` is an exact multiple of contentHeight the remainder is 0, so the last page is reported as entirely free and a referral is promised a place under a letter whose last page is in fact full — the one direction supervisor ruling (4) asks the estimate never to err in.
findings.fix: Treat a zero remainder from a non-empty document as a full page: `var remainder = used % contentHeight; var usedOnLast = used <= contentHeight && breaks == 0 ? used : (remainder == 0 && used > 0 ? contentHeight : remainder);`

findings.issue: IDerivedDocumentBuilder and ILetterDocumentStore are not registered, so DerivedDocumentBuilder — a deliverable of this package's spec row (AGREEMENT item 31) — is unreachable in the running application and TemplateService always resolves a null vault, meaning a real installation that received an organisation template in its setup file still composes on the built-in one. The builder reported this as deferred to B3-2, which owns the vault, and it is correctly built and tested here.
findings.fix: No change in this package. B3-2 must register its vault as ILetterDocumentStore and add `services.AddSingleton<IDerivedDocumentBuilder, DerivedDocumentBuilder>();` beside the B3-1b block; carry this forward as an explicit acceptance item of B3-2.

findings.issue:
The_template_s_padding_does_not_push_the_closing_phrase_onto_a_second_page asserts `Occurrences(printed, "

") <= 3`, which is weaker than the behaviour it documents (a run of blanks becomes ONE blank line) and would keep passing if the collapse regressed to emitting up to three.
findings.fix:
Assert against a template built for the purpose — TemplateBuilder.WithLines(body mark, "", "", "", "", closing phrase) — and require exactly one `

` between the body and the closing phrase.
